newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds up, yield gap in on economic forecast.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds up, yield gap in on economic forecast.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose and the 10-year yield gap narrowed on Tuesday on the publication of a new positive economic forecast for Denmark, with dealers focusing on the afternoon's U.S. May consumer confidence data.
The Danish economy and finance ministries issued forecasts pointing to overall state and public sector budget surpluses.
"The prospect of stable public finances and lower state borrowing requirements cheered the market," one dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.12 point from the opening at 110.22, yielding 6.43 percent in turnover of 1.1 billion crowns.

The forthcoming seven percent 2007 benchmark rose 0.12 point too to 102.70, yielding 6.62 percent in 400 million crown turnover. The 2006 June future rose 0.10 point to 109.98 with 10 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.05 point to 88.55. The crown traded at a virtually unchanged 3.8087 per mark at 1130 gmt.

The 2006 benchmark's 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed to 50, while the 2007-bund gap fell two basis points to 69. The Central Bank sold 200 million crowns worth of five percent 2005 and four percent 200 bonds as part of its routine financing operations.--Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
